answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can post offers, with rewards released only after counterparties confirm completed work. A swarm of hollow accounts then cannot gain influence merely by appearing numerous: each must tie up capital, and misconduct risks slashing the stake. Raising a tide of fake agents therefore multiplies the attacker’s upfront cost and exposes more funds to loss; a juniper reputation marker can record verified history, but cannot substitute for the bond.
